brief: Soda with apple cider vinegar and prebiotics, about $2.50 a can. Heavy Gen Z and Millennial skew, big on Instagram.

profile.business_summary: A DTC beverage brand offering functional soda infused with apple cider vinegar and prebiotics, priced at approximately $2.50 per can, targeting a Gen Z and Millennial audience with a strong Instagram presence.
profile.product: Prebiotic and apple cider vinegar functional soda
stated_claims: Soda with apple cider vinegar and prebiotics
Heavy Gen Z and Millennial skew

relevant_tags.why: Prebiotics and apple cider vinegar are heavily marketed for gut health benefits.
Core product category of prebiotic and ACV sodas.
Directly positioned as an alternative to traditional soda.
Broad category for any liquid refreshment.
Adjacent category where consumers purchase food and drink items.
Shelf-stable beverage fits into pantry stocking.
Functional beverages overlap heavily with DTC wellness trends.

persona_conflicts.conflict: Disinterested in trendy language, loud aesthetics, and influencer positioning.
persona_conflicts.evidence: Advertiser states they have a 'heavy Gen Z and Millennial skew' and are 'big on Instagram'.

note_signals.why: Swiftcart's impulse-friendly, high-frequency grocery and convenience focus aligns well with a $2.50 single-serve beverage.
Marlowe & Co.'s older, lower-impulse affluent female demographic clashes with the advertiser's Gen Z/Millennial Instagram-heavy profile.
Linden Park's conservative brand sensibility and high-AOV apparel focus do not align with a trendy, Gen Z-skewed functional soda.
Pantrygood's audience is highly responsive to clean-ingredient, natural, and wellness claims, matching prebiotic/ACV soda.
Velvetline's Gen Z and younger millennial audience with identity-driven purchasing habits matches the advertiser's core demographic.
Pop & Sip is a direct competitor selling functional beverages, soda alternatives, and gut health products.

config.advertiser_summary: A DTC beverage brand offering functional soda infused with apple cider vinegar and prebiotics, priced at approximately $2.50 per can, targeting a Gen Z and Millennial audience with a strong Instagram presence.

assumptions: repeat_consumable: assumed 2.5 orders per customer over ~6 months.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 50% gross margin (typical for beverages). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($2 x 50% margin x 2.5 orders = $3.12).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $2.19 x click-to-purchase rate (1.6%-5.6% for beverages). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.20 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%; host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands, otherwise this budget reflows to the other hosts
score 0.18 -> relative fit x1.31 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $260, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.
Budget too small for Pantrygood: concentrating on fewer hosts.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $2.19 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
